beats.title: Pascal's Five-Sol Coaches in Paris
beats.description: Horse-drawn coaches ran fixed routes across Paris for a flat low fare, the first scheduled public urban transport.

beats.title: Swansea and Mumbles Passenger Cars
beats.description: Horse-drawn cars began carrying fare-paying passengers along the Welsh shore, the first regular passenger rail service anywhere.

beats.title: Shillibeer's London Omnibus
beats.description: A coachbuilder started a horse-drawn omnibus carrying many passengers between Paddington and the Bank in London.

beats.title: New York's Horse-Drawn Streetcar
beats.description: Horse-drawn cars on iron rails began carrying New Yorkers along the Bowery, the first street railway in the world.
beats.note: New York and Harlem Railroad's first horsecar line, 1832.

beats.title: Birkenhead Street Tramway
beats.description: An American entrepreneur laid grooved rails along a Merseyside street, bringing horse trams to Britain.

beats.title: London Underground Opens
beats.description: Steam trains began running beneath London's streets between Paddington and Farringdon, the world's first underground railway.

beats.title: San Francisco's First Cable Car
beats.description: A cable-hauled car successfully made its first run down a steep hill, launching the city's famous cable car system.

beats.title: Lichterfelde Electric Tram
beats.description: Werner von Siemens ran the world's first electric tram in a Berlin suburb, powered through the running rails.

beats.title: Richmond Electric Streetcars
beats.description: A Virginia city opened the first large-scale electric streetcar network, proving trolleys could climb hills and carry crowds.

beats.title: London's First Electric Deep Tube
beats.description: Electric locomotives began hauling passengers through deep, circular tunnels beneath London, ending smoky underground travel.

beats.title: Budapest Metro Opens
beats.description: The first underground railway on the European mainland opened under a grand avenue as part of a national celebration.

beats.title: Paris Metro Opens
beats.description: The first line of the Paris Metro began carrying passengers beneath the capital as visitors flocked to a world fair.

beats.title: New York Subway Opens
beats.description: Crowds rode the city's first underground line from City Hall to Harlem on a gala evening, launching the New York subway.

beats.title: Buenos Aires Subte Opens
beats.description: The first underground line in Latin America and the Southern Hemisphere began running beneath the Argentine capital.

beats.title: Madrid Metro Opens
beats.description: The king inaugurated a short underground line in Madrid, the start of what became one of Europe's largest metro networks.

beats.title: Barcelona Metro Opens
beats.description: The Gran Metro began carrying passengers beneath Barcelona, on a short line running up from the city centre.

beats.title: Tokyo's Ginza Line Opens
beats.description: Asia's first subway opened in Tokyo with a short stretch of track between Ueno and Asakusa.

beats.title: Osaka Subway Opens
beats.description: Osaka opened its first subway line, which grew into one of Japan's busiest transit networks.

beats.title: Moscow Metro Opens
beats.description: The Soviet capital opened its first underground line, with marble halls and chandeliers intended as palaces for the people.

beats.title: Toronto's Yonge Subway Opens
beats.description: Canada's first subway line opened beneath Yonge Street, carrying commuters in the Toronto downtown.

beats.title: Rome Metro Opens
beats.description: Rome opened its first metro line, built slowly because ancient ruins lay beneath the streets.

beats.title: Montreal Metro Opens
beats.description: Montreal opened a rubber-tyred metro with art-filled stations, ahead of a world exposition.

beats.title: Mexico City Metro Opens
beats.description: Mexico City began running trains on its first line, with pictogram station icons so riders who could not read could navigate.

beats.title: Curitiba's Bus Rapid Transit
beats.description: A Brazilian city launched dedicated bus lanes with raised tube stations, a model copied by cities worldwide.

beats.title: Washington Metro Opens
beats.description: The American capital opened the first stretch of its vaulted-ceiling metro system.

beats.title: Hong Kong MTR Opens
beats.description: Hong Kong began running trains on its first Mass Transit Railway line beneath Kowloon.

beats.title: Vancouver SkyTrain Opens
beats.description: A driverless, automated light metro began running through Vancouver, opened in time for a world fair.

beats.title: Singapore MRT Opens
beats.description: Singapore's first Mass Rapid Transit trains carried passengers on a short stretch of a new island-wide network.

beats.title: Shanghai Metro Opens
beats.description: Shanghai opened its first subway line, the start of what became the longest metro network in the world.

beats.title: Bogota's TransMilenio Opens
beats.description: Bogota launched a high-capacity bus rapid transit system with express lanes, inspired by the Curitiba model.

beats.title: Delhi Metro Opens
beats.description: Delhi began metro service with a first line, starting a rapid expansion across the Indian capital.

beats.title: Dubai Metro Opens
beats.description: Dubai opened a driverless metro, then the longest automated rail network in the world, running through the desert city.

beats.title: Sydney Metro Opens
beats.description: Sydney began operating its first fully automated, driverless metro line in the north-west of the city.

beats.title: London's Elizabeth Line Opens
beats.description: A long-awaited cross-London railway through deep central tunnels opened to passengers, named for the late monarch.
